Each has Lvl2 mechanisms and Lvl3 predictions with numeric thresholds. - **H1, epochs to target:** the main lever is cutting the number of epochs needed for 75%. Mechanisms:   - an airbench96-style backbone with whitening and Dirac init;   - Muon for the conv filters;   - label smoothing 0.3 plus Lookahead/EMA;   - alternating flip, which should matter more because test-time augmentation is banned. - **H2, cost per epoch:**   - keep data on the GPU and augment there, which matters a lot with only 4 CPU cores;   - a vectorised optimizer, compiled step, fp16 with channels_last, and CUDA graphs;   - progressive resizing 24→28→32 px;   - hard-example filtering with a proxy model (low prior). - **H3, fixed timed overhead:**   - compile or autotune leaking out of build when a shape wasn't warmed up;   - the cost of prepare() itself. - **H4, accuracy margin:**   - seed and time noise; a 3-seed mean below about 0.756 is fragile for the 40-seed judgment;   - near 9 epochs, epoch count trades smoothly against margin. Suggested order of experiments: 1. Run the unmodified template twice to measure noise (H4.1.1). 2. Test GPU-resident data on the template (H2.1.1), so data-pipeline gains aren't mixed up with architecture changes. 3. Port the airbench96-style net at 9 epochs with LS 0.3 (H1.1.1). The PR's reference to beat is about 8.1 s, but at 75.29% it is below our 0.753 bar. 4. Only then try Muon, progressive resizing and systems work, one change per run. Every run needs a compliance check: eval timed at B = 1, 7, 512 and 1024, no real data used in build, and every training shape warmed up in build. So any time cut is close to a coin flip on the local 0.753 bar. Two rules follow: - Every idea near the bar is also judged on held-out seeds 3–12, not only on seeds 0–2. - No idea re-rolls the random-number streams to chase a lucky seeds 0–2 result. That would be overfitting to the three test seeds. **New ideas, highest priority first:** 1. **Cut 0.5 epoch (H4.2.4, priority 5).** This is the untested half-epoch point; E020 only tried a full epoch. Expected: about −5% time (to about 6.2 s), with a held-out mean of about 0.755–0.757. 2. **26 px instead of 28 px in the middle phase (priority 3).** This tests one committee member's idea that the accuracy cost of low resolution depends on whether the last feature map ends up 3×3 or 2×2, not on pixel count. Swapping 28 px for 26 px keeps the 3×3 map. Expected: about −4% time; if that idea is right, a loss of 0.15 pp or less. 3. **Stronger weight averaging (H1.3, priority 3).** Change the averaging ramp exponent from 3 to 2, so averaging pulls harder from mid-run on. It costs no time and could pay for trims, which another member flagged as a key open question. 4. **Lower label smoothing at low resolution (H2.3.4, priority 2).** Use 0.15 during the 24/28 px phases and keep 0.3 at 32 px. It should explain why narrowing group 2 in E021 saved only half the expected time, and whether a lossless kernel fix exists. 6. **Hard-example selection with a small proxy net (H2.4.1, priority 1).** This is the one large lever not yet explored, so it is a long shot.
